Unfortunately, I was told that the only way to get an appointment is to phone at 8:30 am then the doctor will phone back during the day to triage my case. As someone with a fulltime job, this is completely impractical. Firstly, I start work at 8:30 am so, just going into the practice to register this morning, meant I was running almost an hour late and worked through my lunch hour. Secondly, if I am in meetings or out on a farm with a client, I cannot abruptly leave to answer the phone.

I was told by the receptionist that, if I’m genuinely ill, I would make time. I find this rather insulting given that I had just explained that my period has been going on for roughly 3 months. I appreciate this isn’t a medical emergency. I don’t need to go to A&E or call an ambulance or even have a same day appointment, but it is clearly abnormal and requires further investigation.

I appreciate that a lot changed during COVID. However, most areas are returning to normal except GP surgeries which seem to be stuck in a COVID mentality. The ripple effects of this are huge. I have been trying (unsuccessfully) to see a doctor for over a month. The only way to achieve this seems to be to inconvenience my employer, my colleagues, and my clients, as I won't be able to provide any indication of when the doctor will phone during the day. The new system may be an improvement for some, but it is wildly impractical for others. The NHS should be accessible to everyone; not just the retired, the unemployed and stay at home mums that have a high degree of flexibility. At the end of the day, everyone that works and pays taxes helps keep the NHS running so we should be able to access its services. The current system needs to be more flexible and offer a range of access routes depending on a person’s circumstances.

Firstly, an online form to give medical history rather than phoning in would allow a working person to fill-in the form before work so they wouldn’t start the day by running late. It would also save receptionist time and make it easier for others phoning in as their call would be answered quicker.

Secondly, giving clients the option of different types of triage appointments, not just phone calls but also text message, email, or whats app. If the medical history from the online form isn’t sufficient to triage the case, the doctor could request further information via text, whats app or email. This allows the client to respond at a time that is convenient to them rather than being expected to drop everything at an unspecified time with the related consequences.

Thirdly, allowing a variety of appointment times including daytime, evening and weekends that are both same day and later in the week so that people can see the GP around work and provide their employer and clients with sufficient notice. At the end of the day, this is standard at most vet practices.
